To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a decrease in total income of all contributors can lead to a higher level of the public good, and that the provision level can be increased without improving the welfare of all contributors.

a redistribution away (toward) a contributor (non-contributor) and a reduction (increase) of the total wealth can lead to an (increase) decrease in the provided level (of a public good) and that a Pareto improving intervention is possible.

the standard neutrality results are not robust in a model with production and relative price effects, and that, in our model, the standard results of non-neutrality are not sufficient to guarantee the existence of Pareto improving policy interventions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to design policy interventions to increase the provision of a public good in a model with production.
the question: How much public good should be provided at a given subscription equilibrium?
the question of what policy instruments may lead to an increase of the public good level in a subscription equilibrium, and whether the resulting increase in utility is Pareto efficient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the public good level in the economy is not a sufficient statistic for the well-being of all agents in the economy, and that the well-being of a subset of the agents is not a sufficient condition for the well-being in the entire economy.
a redistribution of income away from contributors may be welfare-improving, while a redistribution towards contributors may be welfare-decreasing.
, in our model, the standard neutrality result holds for some economies and not for others, while the standard suboptimality result holds in general.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the non-neutrality results of the standard model of a public good with one private good do not carry over to the model with many private good and relative price effects.
the non-neutrality of policy instruments is a more general feature of the model than the neutrality result.

the standard neutrality result of public good models with a single private good does not hold in a model with many private good inputs and relative price effects, and the standard constrained suboptimality result of public good model does not hold if the production technology is not linear in private good inputs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neutrality of redistribution is not a generic feature of the subscription equilibrium.
a non-neutrality of the redistribution of private goods in terms of the provided public good level and the welfare of all households can occur in a general equilibrium model.
the standard neutrality results in the literature are not robust to the presence of production of public goods and the resulting relative price effects.
